Welcome to one of the most distinctive chapters in this predominantly technical book, where we set forth on a journey through the nuanced landscapes of culture, society, and law that mold the era of personalized AI, powered by LLMs. In this chapter, enriched with in-depth discussions, you’ll delve into the dynamic interplay between technology and society, examining how sociocultural factors shape the development and adoption of generative AI. Furthermore, you’ll traverse the existing and emerging legal frameworks that govern these technologies, unraveling the complexities and implications they entail with real-world examples. Join us as we navigate this multifaceted terrain, striving to comprehend and navigate the challenges and opportunities presented by AI in our contemporary world.

欢迎来到这本以技术为主的书中最具特色的一章。在本章里，我们将穿行于文化、社会与法律这三个交织的领域，它们共同塑造了由 LLM 驱动的个性化 AI 时代。你将深入探讨技术与社会之间的动态相互作用，并借助真实案例梳理现有与新兴法律框架所带来的复杂意涵。

A New Kind of Socio-Technical Systems 一种新型的社会技术系统

Socio-technical systems are complex systems that involve the interaction of people, technology, processes, structures, and culture to achieve specific goals. These systems are characterized by the interdependence and interconnectedness of their components, where changes in one component can have significant impacts on the others.

社会技术系统是由人、技术、流程、结构与文化相互作用以达成特定目标的复杂系统。其特点是各要素彼此依赖、相互关联，任一要素的变化都会对其他要素产生显著影响。

In this brave new world of generative AI, we find ourselves at the frontier of a new and transformative kind of socio-technical system, one where the boundaries between technology and society are increasingly blurred, and one that is fundamentally reshaping the way we interact with technology and each other. Unlike traditional socio-technical systems, where technology is a tool used by people to achieve specific goals, generative AI systems are becoming active participants in shaping our social interactions, cultural norms, and even our sense of self.

在生成式 AI 这一崭新世界中，我们正站在一种变革性新型社会技术系统的前沿：技术与社会的边界日益模糊，它从根本上重塑着我们与技术、以及彼此之间的互动方式。传统社会技术系统里技术只是人达成目标的工具，而生成式 AI 正成为塑造我们社交、文化规范乃至自我认知的主动参与者。

— PDF 第 260 页 —

Imagine a world where your virtual assistant knows you better than your closest friends, anticipating your needs and desires with uncanny accuracy. Where the news articles you read and the social media posts you see are generated by AI systems that have learned to mimic human language and creativity. Where the very notion of “human” and “machine” becomes harder to distinguish.

想象这样一个世界：你的虚拟助手比挚友更懂你，以惊人的准确度预判你的需求与渴望；你读的新闻、刷到的社媒帖子都由学会模仿人类语言与创造力的 AI 生成；“人”与“机器”的概念愈发难以分辨。

This is the world we are rapidly moving toward, and it raises profound questions about the nature of our relationship with technology. Are these AI systems merely tools, or are they something more? How do we maintain our agency and autonomy in a world where algorithms shape our choices and perceptions? And what are the implications for privacy, security, and social inequality as these systems become more integrated into the fabric of our daily lives?

这正是我们快速逼近的世界，它引出了关于人与技术关系本质的深刻问题：AI 仅仅是工具，还是不止于此？当算法塑造我们的选择与感知时，我们如何保住能动性与自主性？当这些系统更深地织入日常生活，又会给隐私、安全与社会不平等带来怎样的影响？

To understand how generative AI is transforming socio-technical systems, we can examine its impact on the six main components of these systems:

要理解生成式 AI 如何改变社会技术系统，我们可以从它对该系统六大组成部分的影响入手。

  • People — The roles and relationships of people within socio-technical systems are being reshaped by generative AI. As these systems become more sophisticated in their ability to mimic human language and behavior, they are taking on new roles as social agents, collaborators, and even companions. This shift raises questions about the nature of human identity and agency in an AI-mediated world.

    人（People）—生成式 AI 正在重塑社会技术系统中人的角色与关系。随着系统模仿人类语言与行为的能力日益精进，它们正扮演起社会行动者、协作者乃至陪伴者的新角色。这一转变引出了 AI 中介世界中人类身份与能动性本质的追问。

  • Processes — Generative AI is transforming the processes and workflows involved in various domains, from content creation and curation to decision-making and problem-solving. By automating complex tasks and providing intelligent assistance, these systems are streamlining processes and enabling new forms of creativity and innovation.

    流程（Processes）—生成式 AI 正在改变各领域的流程与工作流，从内容创作与策展到决策制定与问题解决。通过自动化复杂任务并提供智能辅助，这些系统精简了流程，并催生了新的创造力与创新形态。

  • Culture — The increasing prevalence of generative AI is giving rise to new cultural norms, expectations, and values. As these systems become more integrated into our daily lives, they are influencing the way we communicate, consume information, and form our beliefs and opinions. This shift raises important questions about the role of AI in shaping our cultural landscape and the potential for algorithmic bias and manipulation.

    文化（Culture）—生成式 AI 的日益普及正在催生新的文化规范、期待与价值观。当它们更深地融入日常生活，便会影响我们沟通、消费信息、形成信念与观点的方式。这引出了 AI 在形塑文化图景中的角色，以及算法偏见与操纵之虞等重要问题。

  • Structure — Generative AI is also influencing the organizational structures and power dynamics within socio-technical systems. As these systems become more autonomous and capable, they are challenging traditional hierarchies and decision-making processes. This shift raises questions about accountability, transparency, and the distribution of power and control within these systems.

    结构（Structure）—生成式 AI 也在影响社会技术系统中的组织结构与权力动态。随着系统日益自主、能力日益强大，它们正在挑战传统层级与决策流程。这引出了问责、透明，以及系统内权力与控制权分配等问题。

  • Technology — At the core of this transformation is the technology of generative AI itself, which is advancing at an unprecedented pace. From large language models and generative adversarial networks to reinforcement learning and multimodal systems, the capabilities of these technologies are expanding rapidly, enabling new forms of creativity, problem-solving, and social interaction.

    技术（Technology）—这一变革的核心正是生成式 AI 技术本身，其正以前所未有的速度演进。从大语言模型、生成对抗网络到强化学习与多模态系统，这些技术的能力迅速扩展，催生了新的创造力、问题求解与社会互动形态。

  • Goals — Generative AI is redefining the goals and objectives of socio-technical systems by enabling highly personalized and context-aware experiences. These systems can adapt to individual preferences and needs, creating tailored content, recommendations, and interactions that blur the lines between human and machine agency.

    目标（Goals）—生成式 AI 通过实现高度个性化、上下文感知的体验，正在重新定义社会技术系统的目的与目标。系统可因人而异，量身定制内容、推荐与互动，从而模糊人类能动性与机器能动性之间的界限。

这意味着在 AI 发展与治理上采用更整体、跨学科的路径，把社会、文化与政治维度纳入考量；意味着让更广泛的利益相关者——从伦理学家、社会科学家到受影响的社区与公众——参与塑造个性化 AI 的未来；也意味着在这片新疆域中，敢于提出尖锐问题、挑战我们对何为可能、可欲与合德的既有假设。

Riding Amidst an AI-Mediated Cultural Evolution 驾驭 AI 中介下的文化演进

As personalized AI systems become more integrated into our daily lives, they are not just changing the way we interact with technology, but instead, are also fundamentally reshaping our culture and society. From the way we communicate and consume information to the way we work and create, AI is mediating and transforming every aspect of our lives.

随着个性化 AI 系统更深地融入日常生活，它们不仅改变了我们与技术互动的方式，更在从根本上重塑我们的文化与社会。从沟通、信息消费到工作与创作，AI 正在中介并改造我们生活的方方面面。

The Rise of AI-Generated Content and the Erosion of Trust AI 生成内容的兴起与信任的侵蚀

One of the most visible ways this is happening is through the proliferation of AI-generated content. Already, we are seeing the rise of highly realistic videos and images generated by AI that blur the line between reality and fiction. As these technologies become more advanced and accessible, they have the potential to revolutionize fields like entertainment, journalism, and education by enabling new forms of creativity and expression, it also raises significant concerns about the erosion of trust and the spread of misinformation, as well as thorny questions about authenticity and the nature of truth itself.

这一变化最显而易见的体现之一，就是 AI 生成内容的泛滥。我们已经看到高度逼真的 AI 生成视频与图像模糊了真实与虚构的边界。随着技术愈发先进易得，它们有望革新娱乐、新闻与教育等领域，催生新的创造与表达；但同时也引发了对信任侵蚀、错误信息传播，以及真实性与真理本质等棘手问题的深切担忧。

Deepfakes, for example, can be used to create highly realistic but fake videos of public figures saying or doing things they never actually did, with potentially devastating consequences for public discourse and democracy. Real-world examples of this phenomenon are already emerging, such as the use of AI-generated fake news articles and social media posts to influence political opinions and voting behavior. As these

例如，深度伪造可用来制作高度逼真、却纯属虚构的视频，让公众人物说过、做过他们从未说过做过的事，可能对公共讨论与民主造成毁灭性后果。此类现象的现实案例已经出现，比如用 AI 生成的假新闻与社媒帖子来左右政治观点与投票行为。随着这些

techniques become more sophisticated and accessible, the challenge of distinguishing between truth and fiction in an AI-mediated world becomes increasingly daunting.

技术愈发精巧、门槛愈发降低，在 AI 中介的世界里辨别真相与虚构的挑战也愈发艰巨。

Personalized AI and Identity Crisis in the Age of Surveillance Capitalism 监控资本主义时代的个性化 AI 与身份危机

Another critical aspect of the AI-mediated cultural evolution is the impact of personalized AI on individual identity and privacy. In the age of surveillance capitalism, personal data has become a valuable commodity, with companies using AI-powered systems to collect, analyze, and monetize vast amounts of information about our online behaviors, preferences, and interactions.

AI 中介文化演进的另一个关键方面，是个性化 AI 对个人身份与隐私的冲击。在监控资本主义时代，个人数据已成宝贵商品，企业借助 AI 系统收集、分析并变现海量关于我们在线行为、偏好与互动的信息。

This constant surveillance and profiling of individuals raises profound questions about the nature of identity and agency in an AI-mediated world. As our online experiences become increasingly curated by algorithms that learn from our data, we risk becoming trapped in “echo chambers” and “filter bubbles” that reinforce our existing beliefs and limit our exposure to diverse perspectives.

这种对个人的持续监视与画像，引出了 AI 中介世界中身份与能动性本质的深刻问题。当我们的在线体验越来越被从数据中学习的算法所策展，我们就可能困在“回音室”与“过滤气泡”中，既强化既有信念，又限制接触多元观点。

Moreover, the increasing reliance on AI-powered recommendation systems and personalization algorithms can lead to a phenomenon we might call “algorithmic identity” or “AI-mediated selfhood,” where our sense of self and our understanding of the world around us are shaped by the outputs of these systems. This raises concerns about the erosion of personal autonomy, the manipulation of individual preferences and behaviors, and the amplification of social polarization and inequality.

此外，对 AI 推荐系统与个性化算法的日益依赖，可能导致一种可称为“算法身份”或“AI 中介自我”的现象——我们的自我认知与对周遭世界的理解都被这些系统的输出所塑造。这引发了对个人自主被侵蚀、个体偏好与行为被操纵、社会两极分化与不平等被放大的担忧。

Existential Questions in Human-Machine Interaction 人机交互中的存在性追问

As AI systems become more sophisticated in their ability to mimic human language and behavior, the boundaries between human and machine interaction are becoming increasingly blurred. This trend raises profound existential questions about the nature of humanity and our relationship with technology. Already, many of us interact with chatbots and virtual assistants on a daily basis, often without even realizing it. As these systems become more sophisticated and personalized, they have the potential to fundamentally alter the nature of our social relationships and even our sense of self.

随着 AI 模仿人类语言与行为的能力愈发精细，人机交互的边界日益模糊。这一趋势引出了关于人性本质及人与技术关系的深刻存在性追问。我们中许多人每天都在与聊天机器人、虚拟助手互动，却常常浑然不觉。当这些系统更精细、更个性化，就有可能从根本上改变我们社会关系乃至自我认知的性质。

Philosophers, ethicists, and futurists have long been fascinated with the implications of AI for human identity and agency. Some argue that the development of truly intelligent machines could challenge our understanding of what it means to be human, as these systems become capable of exhibiting qualities like creativity, empathy, and self-awareness that were once considered uniquely human.

哲学家、伦理学家与未来学家长期以来都着迷于 AI 对人类身份与能动性的意涵。有人认为，真正智能机器的发展会挑战我们对“何以为人”的理解，因为这些系统开始展现出创造力、共情与自我意识等曾被视为人类独有的品质。

Others worry about the potential for AI systems to manipulate or deceive humans, or to be used in ways that violate our fundamental rights and freedoms. But perhaps the most profound cultural impact of personalized AI is the way it is changing our

另一些人则担忧 AI 可能操纵或欺骗人类，或以侵犯基本权利与自由的方式被使用。但个性化 AI 最深远的文化影响，或许在于它正在改变我们

As AI systems become more autonomous and capable, we are increasingly ceding control and decision-making power to algorithms that we may not fully understand or control. This raises urgent questions about accountability, transparency, and the role of human agency in an AI-driven world.

与技术本身的关系。随着 AI 系统愈发自主强大，我们正把控制权与决策权日益让渡给那些我们未必充分理解或掌控的算法。这就迫切引出了问责、透明，以及人类能动性在 AI 驱动世界中扮演何种角色等问题。

Unveiling the Generative AI Supply Chain 揭开生成式 AI 供应链的面纱

To fully understand the cultural implications of generative AI, it is important to examine the entire generative AI supply chain involved in the creation and deployment of these systems. This supply chain can be broken down into the following eight key stages:

要完整理解生成式 AI 的文化意涵，就必须审视这些系统从创建到部署所涉及的整条供应链。该供应链可分解为以下八个关键阶段。

  • Production of creative works — The creation of the raw material (e.g., text, images, videos) that will be used to train generative AI models.

    创作作品生产—创作将用于训练生成式 AI 模型的原材料（如文本、图像、视频）。

  • Conversion of creative works into quantified data — The process of transforming these creative works into structured datasets that can be used for machine learning.

    作品量化为数据—将这些作品转化为可用于机器学习的结构化数据集的过程。

  • Creation and curation of training datasets — The selection and preparation of specific datasets to train generative AI models for particular tasks or domains.

    训练数据集的创建与策展—为特定任务或领域挑选并准备特定数据集，用以训练生成式 AI 模型。

  • Base model (pre-)training — The initial training of large-scale generative AI models on broad datasets to capture general patterns and relationships.

    基座模型（预）训练—在广泛数据集上对大规模生成式 AI 模型进行初始训练，以捕捉通用模式与关系。

  • Model fine-tuning — The adaptation of pre-trained models to specific problem domains or use cases through additional training on specialized datasets.

    模型微调—通过在专业数据集上追加训练，将预训练模型适配到特定问题领域或用例。

  • Model release or deployment — The integration of trained models into software systems or platforms for use by end users or customers.

    模型发布或部署—将训练好的模型集成进软件系统或平台，供终端用户或客户使用。

  • Generation — The use of trained models to generate new content or outputs based on user prompts or input data, which can in turn be used as training data for (pre)-training and fine-tuning and production of creative works to a certain degree.

    生成—基于用户提示或输入数据，用训练好的模型生成新内容或输出；这些输出在一定程度上又可反过来作为（预）训练、微调的数据，并成为新的创作素材。

  • Alignment — The ongoing process of adjusting and optimizing models and systems to better align with specific goals or values (e.g., accuracy, safety, fairness).

    对齐—持续调整与优化模型和系统，使其更好地契合特定目标或价值（如准确性、安全、公平）。

— PDF 第 265 页 —

Each stage of this supply chain involves critical choices and decisions that can have significant implications for the cultural impact and ethical risks of generative AI.1 For example, the selection and curation of training datasets can introduce biases or skew the outputs of these systems in particular directions, while the deployment and use of these systems can raise questions about intellectual property rights, attribution, and liability.

这条供应链的每一阶段都牵涉关键选择与决策，会对生成式 AI 的文化影响与伦理风险产生重大影响。例如，训练数据的挑选与策展可能引入偏见、或把系统输出带向特定方向；而系统的部署与使用则会引出知识产权、署名与责任归属等问题。

Each stage involves critical choices and decisions that shape the cultural impact and ethical implications of generative AI.

The Emergence of Machine Culture 机器文化的兴起

As generative AI systems become more integrated into our cultural landscape, we are witnessing the emergence of a new form of culture that is mediated and even generated by machines. This machine culture represents a fundamental transformation of the processes of cultural evolution, as intelligent systems begin to play a more active role in shaping the creation, transmission, and selection of cultural artifacts and practices.2

随着生成式 AI 系统更深地进入我们的文化图景，我们正目睹一种由机器中介乃至生成的新型文化兴起。这种“机器文化”代表着文化演进过程的根本转型——智能系统开始在文化产物与实践的创造、传递与选择中扮演更主动的角色。

One key aspect of this transformation is the increasing influence of algorithmic curation and recommendation systems on our cultural consumption and production. Platforms like Netflix, Spotify, and YouTube use sophisticated AI algorithms to personalize content recommendations and shape user behavior, effectively acting as gatekeepers and tastemakers for vast coastlines of our cultural landscape.

这一转型的一个关键方面，是算法策展与推荐系统对我们文化消费和生产日益增强的影响。Netflix、Spotify、YouTube 等平台借助精密的 AI 算法个性化内容推荐、塑造用户行为，实际上成了我们辽阔文化图景中的把关人与品味塑造者。

Moreover, as generative AI systems become more advanced, they are beginning to contribute directly to the creation of cultural artifacts and experiences. From AI-generated music and art, to machine-written stories and scripts, these systems are blurring the lines between human and machine creativity, raising questions about the nature of originality, authorship, and intellectual property in an AI-mediated world.

此外，随着生成式 AI 愈发先进，它们开始直接参与文化产物与文化体验的创造。从 AI 生成的音乐与艺术，到机器撰写的故事与剧本，这些系统正模糊人类创造与机器创造的界限，引出 AI 中介世界中原创性、作者身份与知识产权本质的追问。

Ultimately, the goal should be to steer the development and deployment of generative AI systems via a critical and reflective lens in ways that align with our cultural values and priorities, while also harnessing the potential of these technologies to enable new forms of creativity, expression, and social innovation. This means being mindful of the cultural assumptions and biases that are embedded in these systems. The key to riding the wave of AI-mediated cultural change is to remain open, adaptable, and willing to engage in ongoing dialogue and negotiation. As you’ll explore in the following sections, this requires not only technical solutions, but also a fundamental rethinking of our social, legal, and ethical frameworks for governing these powerful new technologies.

归根结底，目标应是带着批判与反思的眼光引导生成式 AI 的发展与部署，使其契合我们的文化价值与优先事项，同时善用这些技术的潜力，催生新的创造、表达与社会创新。这意味着要觉察嵌入系统中的文化假设与偏见。驾驭 AI 中介文化变革浪潮的关键，是保持开放、灵活，并乐于持续对话与协商。正如后续各节将探讨的，这不仅需要技术方案，更需要从根本上重新思考我们用以治理这些强大新技术的社会、法律与伦理框架。

Adaptable Legal Frameworks for Regulation and Accountability 面向监管与问责的适应性法律框架

As personalized AI systems powered by LLMs become increasingly prevalent in our daily lives, the need for robust and adaptable legal frameworks to ensure their responsible development and deployment grows more pressing. In this section, you’ll explore some of the key aspects of the legal and regulatory challenges posed by these technologies and discuss potential approaches for addressing them.

随着 LLM 驱动的个性化 AI 系统在日常生活中愈发普及，建立强健、可适应的法律框架以确保其负责任地发展与部署，这一需求日益迫切。本节将探讨这些技术带来的法律与监管挑战的若干关键方面，并讨论应对之道。

The Case of Copyright and Intellectual Property in the Age of LLMs LLM 时代的版权与知识产权问题

One of the most significant legal challenges surrounding personalized AI systems, particularly those involving generative models, is the question of copyright and intellectual property rights.3 As these systems become more sophisticated in their ability to create novel content, from text and images to music and video, they raise complex questions about ownership, attribution, and, the most commonly debated, fair use.

围绕个性化 AI 系统（尤其是涉及生成式模型者）最重大的法律挑战之一，就是版权与知识产权问题。随着这些系统创作新内容——从文本、图像到音乐、视频——的能力愈发精细，它们引出了关于所有权、署名，以及最常被争论的合理使用等复杂问题。

The first question to answer is: Does generative AI infringe copyrights?

第一个要回答的问题是：生成式 AI 是否侵犯版权？

Footnote: 3. Pamela Samuelson, “Generative AI Meets Copyright,” Science 381, no. 6654 (2023): 158–161.

注释：3. Pamela Samuelson，《生成式 AI 遇上版权》，Science 381, no. 6654 (2023)：158–161。

As briefly discussed in the previous section, the generative AI supply chain involves multiple stages, from data collection and preprocessing, to model training and deployment, each of which raises distinct legal considerations. For example, consider the case of GitHub Copilot, an AI-powered coding assistant that was trained on billions of lines of publicly available code. When it was first released, many developers raised concerns about the potential for copyright infringement, arguing that the system was essentially regurgitating code snippets without proper attribution or licensing. In response, GitHub released a detailed statement outlining its approach to data licensing and intellectual property, which included using only permissively licensed code and providing attribution to original creators wherever possible.

如前一节简要所述，生成式 AI 供应链包含从数据采集与预处理，到模型训练与部署的多个阶段，每个阶段都引发不同的法律考量。以 GitHub Copilot 为例，这个 AI 编程助手是在数十亿行公开代码上训练的。刚发布时，许多开发者担忧其可能侵犯版权，认为它本质上是在不加署名或许可地复述代码片段。作为回应，GitHub 发布了详细声明，阐明其数据许可与知识产权方针，包括仅使用宽松许可的代码、并在可能处为原作者署名。

The issue of copyright infringement by generative AI has also been a concern in the art world, with many artists claiming that these systems are engaging in “art theft.” They argue that by training on vast datasets of copyrighted artworks, generative AI models are essentially reproducing and deriving works from these sources without permission or compensation. This has led to several lawsuits against companies developing and deploying generative AI systems for creative purposes.4

生成式 AI 的版权侵权问题在艺术界同样引发担忧，许多艺术家声称这些系统在进行“艺术剽窃”。他们认为，通过在海量受版权保护的艺术作品数据集上训练，生成式 AI 模型实质上是在未经许可、未付报酬的情况下复制并衍生这些来源的作品。这已导致数起针对开发与部署创作用途生成式 AI 系统公司的诉讼。

These cases share some similarities with prior legal battles over new technologies, such as the Sony Betamax case in the 1980s, which dealt with the legality of home video recording, and the more recent Andy Warhol Foundation v. Goldsmith case, which examined the boundaries of fair use in the context of artistic appropriation. In the Sony case, the Supreme Court ultimately ruled that the manufacturers of video recording devices could not be held liable for copyright infringement committed by users, as long as the devices were capable of substantial noninfringing uses. This established an important precedent for the safe harbor principle, which has been applied to various technologies over the years.

这些案件与以往围绕新技术的法律论战有相似之处，例如 1980 年代关于家庭录像合法性的 Sony Betamax 案，以及近年探讨艺术挪用语境下合理使用边界的 Andy Warhol 基金会诉 Goldsmith 案。在 Sony 案中，最高法院最终裁定：只要录像设备具有实质性的非侵权用途，其制造商便无需为用户的版权侵权负责。这为安全港原则确立了重要先例，多年来被应用于各种技术。

However, our privacy legislation and copyright laws were not built for the digital age and often fall short in addressing the complexities of 21st-century technologies. The nature of generative AI systems raises new challenges for the application of existing legal doctrines. Unlike traditional technologies that simply enable the reproduction or distribution of copyrighted works, generative AI models actively learn from and transform the data they are trained on, blurring the lines between mere copying and original creation. This has led some legal scholars to argue for a reconsideration of copyright law in the age of AI, proposing new frameworks that can better balance the rights of creators with the transformative potential of these technologies.

然而，我们的隐私立法与版权法并非为数字时代而设，往往难以应对 21 世纪技术的复杂性。生成式 AI 系统的特性给既有法律原则的适用带来新挑战。与仅仅复制或传播受版权作品的传统技术不同，生成式 AI 模型会主动从训练数据中学习并转化它，模糊了单纯复制与原创之间的界限。这促使一些法学学者主张在 AI 时代重新审视版权法，提出能更好平衡创作者权利与技术变革潜力的新框架。

Another relevant case to consider is the legal battle in the early 2000s over peer-to-peer file-sharing networks, such as Napster and Grokster. In these cases, the courts grappled with questions of contributory and vicarious liability for copyright

另一个相关案例是 2000 年代初围绕 Napster、Grokster 等点对点文件共享网络的法律之争。在这些案件中，法院纠结于版权的帮助侵权与替代责任

注释：4. Kyle Chayka，《AI 艺术是在剽窃艺术家吗？》，The New Yorker，2023 年 2 月 10 日，链接见原文。

infringement, ultimately holding these services responsible for the infringing activities of their users. However, subsequent services like Grokster attempted to avoid liability by arguing that it had no direct knowledge or control over user activities, and that its technology had substantial noninfringing uses. While this argument was initially successful, the Supreme Court later ruled against Grokster, finding that the company had actively induced and encouraged infringement.

问题，最终判定这些服务需为用户的侵权行为负责。而后来的 Grokster 等服务则试图免责，辩称其对用户活动既无直接知情也无控制，且其技术具有实质性的非侵权用途。这一抗辩起初奏效，但最高法院后来作出不利于 Grokster 的裁决，认定该公司主动引诱并鼓励了侵权。

These cases illustrate the evolving nature of legal doctrines in response to new technologies, and the challenges of balancing innovation with the protection of intellectual property rights. As we move into an era of generative AI, the need for modernized privacy and copyright laws becomes urgent. Developers and deployers may need to consider various strategies to manage and limit their potential copyright liability, such as:

这些案例表明，法律原则会随新技术而演进，也凸显了在创新与知识产权保护之间取得平衡的挑战。随着我们步入生成式 AI 时代，隐私与版权法的现代化已刻不容缓。开发者与部署者可能需要考虑各种策略来管理并限制其潜在版权责任，例如：

  • Intent — Making clear choices about the disaggregation or centralization of AI development and deployment, to avoid the appearance of inducement or direct infringement.

    意图（Intent）—对 AI 开发与部署的分散化或集中化做出清晰选择，以避免出现引诱侵权或直接侵权的表象。

  • Control — Carefully considering the mode of model release and deployment, such as using streaming interfaces or other mechanisms to maintain control over the use and outputs of the system.

    控制（Control）—审慎斟酌模型发布与部署的方式，例如采用流式接口或其他机制，以保持对系统使用与输出的掌控。

  • Knowledge management — Investing in research and development of privacy-preserving technologies, such as encrypted queries and results, to limit the potential for direct knowledge of infringing activities.5

    知情管理（Knowledge management）—投资研发隐私保护技术（如加密的查询与结果），以限制对侵权活动产生直接知情的可能。

These cases also highlight the need for clear and transparent data governance practices in the development of generative AI systems. They also raise important questions about the boundaries of fair use and transformative work in the context of AI-generated content. In the United States, the legal doctrine of fair use allows for the use of copyrighted material without permission in certain circumstances, such as for the purposes of criticism, commentary, or education. However, the application of this doctrine to AI-generated content is still a matter of ongoing legal debate and uncertainty.

这些案例也凸显了在生成式 AI 系统开发中需要清晰、透明的数据治理实践，并引出 AI 生成内容语境下合理使用与转化性作品边界的重要问题。在美国，合理使用原则允许在特定情形下（如批评、评论或教育目的）未经许可使用受版权保护的材料。然而，该原则能否适用于 AI 生成内容，仍是持续争论、尚无定论的法律问题。

The second question to answer is: Do generative AI hold copyrights?

第二个要回答的问题是：生成式 AI 能否持有版权？

Let’s consider another more generic case: the OpenAI’s GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 language models (and their interactive system counterpart, ChatGPT), which were trained on a massive corpus of online text data, including books, articles, and websites. When used to generate new text outputs, these GPT models can produce content that is strikingly similar to human-written prose, leading some to question whether these outputs should be considered original works of authorship or derivative works based on the training data.

再看一个更通用的案例：OpenAI 的 GPT-3.5 与 GPT-4 语言模型（及其交互式系统 ChatGPT），它们在包含书籍、文章与网站的海量在线文本语料上训练。当用于生成新文本时，这些 GPT 模型能产出与人类写作惊人相似的内容，这使一些人质疑：这些输出究竟应被视为原创作品，还是基于训练数据的衍生作品。

The legal status of AI-generated content is still a matter of ongoing debate and uncertainty. In the United States, for example, the Copyright Office has taken the position that works produced by machines without human authorship are not eligible for copyright protection. However, this stance has been challenged by some legal scholars and industry stakeholders, who argue that the human creators of AI systems should be able to claim ownership over the outputs of those systems.

AI 生成内容的法律地位仍是持续争论、尚无定论的问题。例如在美国，版权局的立场是：无人类作者参与、由机器产出的作品不享有版权保护。但这一立场受到部分法学学者与业界利益相关者的挑战，他们主张 AI 系统的人类创造者应能主张对系统输出的所有权。

One approach to determining the originality and copyrightability of AI-generated content is to examine the degree of creativity and genericness involved in the outputs. As the 1991 case of Feist Publications v. Rural Telephone Service established, copyright protection requires a minimal degree of creativity and originality, and does not extend to generic properties or components that are firmly rooted in tradition or expected as a matter of course. This means that elements such as cultural themes, standardized interfaces, artistic styles, and common harmonic progressions may not be protected by copyright.

判定 AI 生成内容的原创性与可版权性的一种思路，是考察输出中所体现的创造性与通用性程度。正如 1991 年 Feist 出版公司诉 Rural 电话公司案所确立的，版权保护要求最低限度的创造性与原创性，并不及于那些深植于传统、或理所当然的通用属性或要素。这意味着文化主题、标准化界面、艺术风格、常见和声进行等要素可能不受版权保护。

Some researchers have proposed using linguistic creativity measures, such as the use of idiomatic expressions, as a way to assess the originality of AI-generated text. By probing the ability of language models to generate novel and noncompositional idioms, it may be possible to distinguish between mere reproduction of training data and genuinely original creation. Similarly, in the domain of AI-generated images, techniques like textual inversion and DreamSim distance for images can be used to evaluate the novelty and originality of generated content.

一些研究者提出用语言创造性指标（如习语表达的使用）来评估 AI 生成文本的原创性。通过探测语言模型生成新颖、非组合性习语的能力，或可区分单纯复现训练数据与真正的原创。类似地，在 AI 图像领域，文本反转、DreamSim 图像距离等技术可用于评估生成内容的新颖性与原创性。

These approaches could potentially be used to support courts in assessing the scope of copyright protection for AI-generated works, as well as to aid copyright owners in negotiating fair licensing deals and policymakers in adapting copyright law to the realities of generative AI. However, much more research and legal analysis is needed to develop clear and consistent frameworks for applying these principles in practice.

这些方法未来或可用于辅助法院判定 AI 生成作品的版权保护范围，也可帮助版权所有者谈判公平许可协议、帮助立法者让版权法适应生成式 AI 的现实。然而，要在实践中形成清晰一致的适用框架，仍需大量研究与法律分析。

Navigating these issues will require a careful balancing of the rights and interests of different stakeholders, from the creators of AI systems, to the owners of the data used to train them, to the end users who interact with the outputs. It will also require the development of new legal frameworks and doctrines that can adapt to the unique characteristics of these technologies, such as their ability to generate outputs based on complex statistical patterns rather than direct human input.

应对这些问题，需要审慎平衡不同利益相关者的权利与利益——从 AI 系统的创造者、训练数据的所有者，到与输出交互的终端用户。这也需要发展出能适配这些技术独特性质的新法律框架与原则，例如它们基于复杂统计模式、而非直接人类输入来生成输出的能力。

The Case of Data Privacy and Protection in Personalized AI Systems 个性化 AI 系统中的数据隐私与保护问题

Another critical legal challenge posed by personalized AI systems is the issue of data privacy and protection. As these systems rely on vast amounts of personal data to train their models and generate tailored outputs, they raise significant concerns about the collection, use, and sharing of sensitive information.

个性化 AI 系统带来的另一个关键法律挑战，是数据隐私与保护问题。由于这些系统依赖海量个人数据来训练模型、生成定制输出，它们引发了对敏感信息收集、使用与共享的重大担忧。

In recent years, we’ve seen a growing push for stronger data privacy regulations around the world, such as the European Union’s General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA). These regulations aim to give individuals greater control over their personal data, impose stricter requirements on companies that collect and process that data, and provide for significant penalties in cases of noncompliance.

近年来，全球范围内要求更强数据隐私监管的呼声日益高涨，例如欧盟的《通用数据保护条例》（GDPR）与加州的《消费者隐私法案》（CCPA）。这些法规旨在让个人对自身数据拥有更大控制权，对收集处理数据的企业施加更严格要求，并对违规处以重罚。

In the healthcare domain, the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) establishes strict rules for the handling of protected health information (PHI) by covered entities and their business associates. This includes requirements for obtaining patient consent, maintaining data security, and providing individuals with access to their own health records. The development and deployment of personalized AI systems in healthcare, such as clinical decision support tools or patient monitoring applications, must carefully navigate these regulations to ensure compliance and protect patient privacy.

在医疗领域，《健康保险流通与责任法案》（HIPAA）为受监管实体及其业务伙伴处理受保护健康信息（PHI）设定了严格规则，包括取得患者同意、维护数据安全、让个人可查阅自身健康记录等要求。在医疗中开发与部署个性化 AI 系统（如临床决策支持工具、患者监测应用），必须谨慎遵循这些法规，确保合规并保护患者隐私。

However, the increasing use of AI systems in healthcare also raises new challenges for data ownership and control. For example, in the case of implantable medical devices like pacemakers or cardioverter defibrillators, manufacturers may claim copyright protection over the software and algorithms used to operate these devices, potentially limiting patients’ ability to access and control their own health data. This issue was highlighted in a series of lawsuits in which patients sought access to the data generated by their implanted devices, but were denied on the grounds that the data was proprietary and protected by the Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA).

然而，AI 系统在医疗中的日益使用，也给数据所有权与控制权带来新挑战。例如，对于起搏器、心律转复除颤器等植入式医疗器械，制造商可能对运行这些设备的软件与算法主张版权保护，从而限制患者获取与控制自身健康数据的能力。这一问题在一系列诉讼中被凸显：患者要求获取植入设备生成的数据，却以数据属专有财产、受《数字千年版权法》（DMCA）保护为由被拒绝。

As AI-powered medical assistants and monitoring systems become more widespread, similar questions of data ownership and control are likely to arise. Patients may find themselves in a position where the data generated by these systems, which could be critical for managing their health and making informed decisions, is owned and controlled by the companies that develop and deploy the technology. This could create significant power imbalances and undermine patient autonomy and privacy.

随着 AI 医疗助手与监测系统更加普及，类似的数据所有权与控制权问题很可能浮现。患者可能发现：那些对管理健康、做出知情决策至关重要的系统数据，其所有权与控制权却掌握在开发和部署该技术的公司手中。这可能造成严重的权力失衡，侵蚀患者的自主与隐私。

For developers and deployers of personalized AI systems, complying with these regulations can be a complex and challenging undertaking. They must ensure that they have obtained appropriate consent from individuals for the collection and use of their data, provide clear and transparent information about their data practices, and implement appropriate security measures to protect against unauthorized access or misuse.

对个性化 AI 系统的开发者与部署者而言，合规是一项复杂而艰巨的任务。他们必须确保已就数据收集与使用取得个人的适当同意，就其数据实践提供清晰透明的说明，并采取适当的安全措施以防未授权访问或滥用。

— PDF 第 271 页 —

At the same time, the use of AI systems can raise new and unique privacy risks that may not be adequately addressed by existing legal frameworks. For example, the ability of these systems to make inferences and predictions about individuals based on patterns in their data, even when that data has been anonymized, can lead to the re-identification of sensitive information and the erosion of privacy protections.

与此同时，AI 系统的使用可能带来现有法律框架难以充分应对的、全新而独特的隐私风险。例如，即便数据已被匿名化，这些系统仍能基于数据中的模式对个人做出推断与预测，这可能导致敏感信息被重新识别，使隐私保护被侵蚀。

Addressing these challenges will require ongoing collaboration among policymakers, industry leaders, and privacy advocates to develop new approaches to data governance and protection that are tailored to the specific risks and opportunities posed by personalized AI systems. This could include the development of new technical standards for data anonymization and encryption, the creation of stronger oversight and accountability mechanisms for AI developers and deployers, and the promotion of greater transparency and public engagement around these issues.

应对这些挑战，需要政策制定者、行业领袖与隐私倡导者持续协作，量身打造适配个性化 AI 特定风险与机遇的数据治理与保护新方法。这包括制定数据匿名化与加密的新技术标准、为 AI 开发者与部署者建立更强的监督与问责机制，并围绕这些议题提升透明度、促进公众参与。

The Case of Algorithmic Bias and Discrimination in AI-Powered Decision Making AI 决策中的算法偏见与歧视问题

A third major legal and ethical challenge posed by personalized AI systems is the risk of algorithmic bias and discrimination in automated decision-making processes. As these systems are increasingly used to make consequential decisions about individuals, from credit and lending to hiring and criminal sentencing, there is a growing concern that they may perpetuate or amplify existing societal biases and inequalities.

个性化 AI 系统带来的第三大法律与伦理挑战，是自动化决策过程中的算法偏见与歧视风险。随着这些系统越来越多地被用于对个人做出影响重大的决策——从信贷发放到招聘与刑事量刑——人们日益担忧它们可能延续甚至放大既有的社会偏见与不平等。

There have been numerous high-profile examples of algorithmic bias in recent years, such as the case of a recidivism risk assessment tool called COMPAS (Correctional Offender Management Profiling for Alternative Sanctions), which was found to be systematically biased against black defendants in the US criminal justice system.6 Similarly, there have been instances of AI-powered hiring tools that have been shown to discriminate against women and minorities, and facial recognition systems that have higher error rates for people with darker skin tones.

近年来已有众多备受瞩目的算法偏见案例，例如再犯风险评估工具 COMPAS（替代制裁的矫正罪犯管理画像）被发现在美国刑事司法体系中系统性地对黑人被告存有偏见。类似地，已有证据表明 AI 招聘工具会歧视女性与少数族裔，人脸识别系统对深色肤色人群的错误率更高。

New York City’s first-of-its-kind law, known as the Bias Audit Law, is designed to combat discrimination that may arise from the use of artificial intelligence when making employment decisions. The law entered its enforcement phase on July 5, 2023, and requires employers to conduct independent bias audits of their automated employment decision tools (AEDTs) and to notify job candidates and employees about the use of these tools in hiring and promotion decisions. Employers must also provide candidates and employees with information about the types of data collected by the AEDTs, the sources of the data, and the job qualifications and characteristics that the AEDTs are intended to measure.

纽约市首创的《偏见审计法》旨在打击就业决策中使用人工智能可能引发的歧视。该法于 2023 年 7 月 5 日进入执法阶段，要求雇主对其自动化就业决策工具（AEDT）进行独立偏见审计，并告知求职者与员工这些工具在招聘与晋升决策中的使用。雇主还须向求职者与员工说明 AEDT 收集的数据类型、数据来源，以及这些工具旨在衡量的岗位资格与特征。

Footnote: 6. Jeff Larson et al., “How We Analyzed the COMPAS Recidivism Algorithm,” ProPublica 9, no. 1 (2016).

注释：6. Jeff Larson 等，《我们如何分析 COMPAS 累犯算法》，ProPublica 9, no. 1 (2016)。

The law reflects a growing recognition of the potential for algorithmic bias and discrimination in AI-powered decision-making systems, and the need for proactive measures to identify and mitigate these risks. By requiring independent audits and increasing transparency around the use of these systems, the law aims to promote greater accountability and fairness in employment practices.

该法律反映出人们日益认识到 AI 决策系统中算法偏见与歧视的可能，以及主动识别并缓解这些风险的必要。通过要求独立审计并提升系统使用的透明度，该法旨在促进就业实践中更强的问责与公平。

However, the effectiveness of the Bias Audit Law and similar regulations will depend on the development of clear standards and best practices for conducting these audits, as well as the creation of enforcement mechanisms to ensure compliance. There are also concerns about the potential limitations of bias audits, such as the difficulty of identifying and measuring all relevant forms of bias, and the risk of creating a false sense of objectivity and fairness in systems that may still have discriminatory outcomes.

然而，《偏见审计法》及类似法规的成效，将取决于能否制定清晰的审计标准与最佳实践，并建立确保合规的执法机制。人们也担忧偏见审计的固有局限，例如难以识别与衡量所有相关形式的偏见，以及在结果仍可能歧视性的系统中制造一种虚假的客观性与公平感。

Addressing these issues will require a multifaceted approach that includes both technical solutions, such as improved data collection and bias testing methods, and legal and policy interventions, such as stronger anti-discrimination laws and oversight mechanisms. It will also require a greater emphasis on diversity and inclusion in the development and deployment of these systems, to ensure that they are designed and used in ways that promote fairness and equality.

解决这些问题需要多管齐下：既要有技术方案（如改进的数据收集与偏见测试方法），也要有法律与政策干预（如更强的反歧视法律与监督机制）。还需在这些系统的开发与部署中更加重视多元与包容，确保其设计与使用能促进公平与平等。

One promising approach is the use of algorithmic impact assessments (AIAs), which are systematic evaluations of the potential risks and harms posed by AI systems in specific contexts. An example of an AIA is presented in Chapter 9. By conducting AIAs throughout the development and deployment process, and involving diverse stakeholders in their design and implementation, developers and deployers can proactively identify and mitigate potential biases and unintended consequences.

一种有前景的做法是采用算法影响评估（AIA），即对 AI 系统在特定情境下可能带来的风险与危害进行系统性评估。第 9 章将给出一个 AIA 实例。通过在开发与部署全过程中开展 AIA、并让多元利益相关者参与其设计与实施，开发者与部署者可主动识别并缓解潜在偏见与意外后果。

However, the effectiveness of AIAs and other governance mechanisms will depend on the development of clear standards and best practices for their use, as well as the creation of stronger incentives and consequences for compliance. This will require ongoing experimentation and learning, as well as a commitment to transparency, accountability, and public engagement in the development and deployment of these systems.

然而，AIA 及其他治理机制的成效，将取决于能否制定清晰的使用标准与最佳实践，并建立更强的合规激励与问责后果。这需要持续试验与学习，也需要在这些系统的开发与部署中坚守透明、问责与公众参与。

The Case of Liability and Accountability in AI-Powered Systems AI 系统中的责任与问责问题

Finally, the use of personalized AI systems raises complex questions around liability and accountability when things go wrong. As these systems become more autonomous and sophisticated in their decision-making capabilities, it can be difficult to determine who is responsible when they cause harm or make mistakes.

最后，个性化 AI 系统的使用在出问题时引出了责任与问责的复杂问题。随着这些系统的决策能力愈发自主、愈发精细，当它们造成损害或犯错时，往往难以判定应由谁负责。

Consider the case of self-driving cars, which rely on complex AI systems to navigate roads and make split-second decisions. If a self-driving car is involved in an accident,

以自动驾驶汽车为例，它依赖复杂的 AI 系统行驶并在瞬间做出决策。若一辆自动驾驶汽车发生事故，

— PDF 第 273 页 —

who is liable? Is it the manufacturer of the car, the developer of the AI system, or the human passenger who was supposed to be monitoring the system?

谁该担责？是汽车制造商、AI 系统开发者，还是本应监控系统的人类乘客？

Similar questions arise in other domains where AI systems are used to make consequential decisions, such as healthcare diagnosis and treatment, financial trading, and government services. In each case, there is a need for clear legal frameworks that can assign responsibility and provide for appropriate remedies and compensation when harms occur.

在其他用 AI 做出重大决策的领域——如医疗诊断与治疗、金融交易、政府服务——也会出现类似问题。每种情形都需要清晰的法律框架，以便在损害发生时划定责任、并提供适当的救济与赔偿。

One approach is to treat AI systems as products, and to apply existing product liability laws to their development and deployment. Under this approach, manufacturers and developers could be held strictly liable for any harms caused by their systems, regardless of fault or negligence. However, this approach may not be well-suited to the unique characteristics of AI systems, which can evolve and change over time based on their interactions with users and the environment.

一种思路是把 AI 系统视为产品，将现有产品责任法适用于其开发与部署。按此思路，制造商与开发者可能需为系统造成的任何损害承担严格责任，不论有无过错或疏忽。但这一思路未必契合 AI 系统的独特性质——它们会随与用户及环境的交互而不断演化变化。

Another approach is to focus on the human operators and decision-makers who deploy and use AI systems, and to hold them accountable for the outcomes of those systems. This could involve the development of new legal doctrines around negligence and duty of care in the context of AI, as well as the creation of stronger oversight and governance mechanisms to ensure that these systems are used responsibly and ethically.

另一种思路是聚焦部署和使用 AI 系统的人类操作者与决策者，让他们为系统的结果负责。这可能需要在 AI 语境下发展关于过失与注意义务的新法律原则，并建立更强的监督与治理机制，确保这些系统被负责任、合乎伦理地使用。

Universal Challenges to Techno-Legal Solutionism 技术-法律解决主义面临的普遍挑战

The legal and regulatory challenges posed by personalized AI systems are complex and multifaceted, and will require ongoing innovation and adaptation to address effectively. From copyright and intellectual property to data privacy and algorithmic bias, these challenges raise fundamental questions about the rights and responsibilities of different stakeholders in the development and deployment of these technologies.

个性化 AI 系统带来的法律与监管挑战复杂而多面，需要持续创新与调适才能有效应对。从版权与知识产权到数据隐私与算法偏见，这些挑战都引出了关于不同利益相关者在技术开发与部署中权利与责任的根本性问题。

One of the key issues that arises in this context is the notion of techno-legal solutionism—the idea that complex social problems can be solved through a combination of technological innovation and legal reform. Techno-legal solutionism often assumes that the challenges posed by AI can be neatly divided into technical and legal categories, and that by developing the right algorithms or passing the right laws, we can effectively mitigate the risks and harness the benefits of these technologies. However, in practice, the technical and legal dimensions of AI governance are deeply intertwined, and addressing them requires a more holistic and interdisciplinary approach.

此中浮现的一个关键问题，是“技术-法律解决主义”——即认为复杂社会问题可通过技术创新与法律改革的结合来解决。技术-法律解决主义往往假设 AI 的挑战可被干净地划分为技术类与法律类，只要开发出对的算法、或通过对的法律，就能有效化解风险、收获收益。但实践中，AI 治理的技术维度与法律维度深度交织，应对它们需要更整体、跨学科的路径。

The first key challenge is the sheer complexity and opacity of many AI systems, which can make it difficult to assign responsibility and enforce accountability when things go wrong. When an AI system makes a decision that harms an individual or a community, who is held liable? The developers who created the system? The companies

首要挑战在于许多 AI 系统本身的极端复杂与不透明，这使得出问题时难以划分责任、落实问责。当一个 AI 系统做出损害个人或社区的决策时，谁该担责？是创造系统的开发者？是部署它的公司？

— PDF 第 274 页 —

that deployed it? The users who interacted with it? The answer is often unclear, and our current legal frameworks are not well-suited to address these thorny questions of accountability in an AI-driven world.

还是与之交互的用户？答案往往并不明朗，而我们现行的法律框架并不擅长应对 AI 驱动世界中这些棘手的问责问题。

Another challenge is the global and cross-jurisdictional nature of many AI systems, which can make it difficult to enforce consistent standards and regulations across borders. When an AI system is developed in one country, deployed in another, and used by individuals all over the world, whose laws and values should it be subject to? How can we ensure that the rights and protections of individuals are respected regardless of where they live or how they interact with these systems?

另一个挑战是许多 AI 系统的全球性与跨法域性，这使得难以跨境执行一致的标准与监管。当一个 AI 系统在一国开发、在另一国部署、被世界各地的人使用时，它应服从谁的法律与价值？我们又如何确保无论个人身处何地、如何与这些系统交互，其权利与保护都得到尊重？

To address these challenges, we need to develop new legal and regulatory frameworks that are adaptable, flexible, and responsive to the rapidly evolving landscape of AI. This may involve creating new laws and policies that are specifically tailored to the unique risks and opportunities posed by AI, as well as updating and reforming existing legal frameworks to better account for the challenges of an AI-driven world.

应对这些挑战，我们需要发展出可适应、灵活、能回应 AI 快速演进图景的新型法律与监管框架。这既可能需要制定专门针对 AI 独特风险与机遇的新法律与政策，也需要更新、改革既有法律框架，以更好地回应 AI 驱动世界的挑战。

One promising approach is to focus on developing principles-based regulations, rather than prescriptive rules that may quickly become outdated as the technology advances. By establishing clear principles and values that should guide the development and deployment of AI systems (such as transparency, fairness, accountability, and privacy), we can create a more adaptable and future-proof regulatory framework that can evolve alongside the technology.

一种有前景的做法是着力发展基于原则的监管，而非那些随技术进步很快过时的命令式规则。通过确立应指导 AI 系统开发与部署的清晰原则与价值（如透明、公平、问责与隐私），我们可以构建一个更具适应性、面向未来的监管框架，使其能与技术共同演进。

But perhaps the most important step we can take is to recognize that the challenges posed by personalized AI are not purely technical or legal in nature—they are deeply intertwined with questions of ethics, values, and power. To truly hold these systems accountable and ensure that they are developed and deployed in ways that benefit society as a whole, we need to engage in ongoing public dialogue and deliberation about the kind of future we want to build with AI.

但或许我们能迈出的最重要一步，是认识到个性化 AI 带来的挑战并非纯技术或纯法律问题——它们与伦理、价值和权力问题深度交织。要真正让这些系统负起责任、确保其发展与部署造福整个社会，我们需要就“想与 AI 共建怎样的未来”开展持续的公共对话与审议。

This means creating new spaces and mechanisms for public participation and input in the development of AI policies and regulations, as well as fostering a culture of transparency and accountability around the use of these technologies. It also means being willing to ask difficult questions and make hard choices about the role we want AI to play in our lives and societies, and the values and principles we want to uphold as we navigate this new frontier.

这意味着在 AI 政策与法规的制定中创设新的公众参与与表达渠道，并围绕这些技术的使用培育透明与问责的文化。也意味着愿意提出尖锐问题，并就“希望 AI 在我们的生活与社会中扮演何种角色、在这片新疆域坚守怎样的价值与原则”做出艰难抉择。

Ultimately, the key to developing adaptable and effective legal frameworks for AI is to approach the challenge with humility, creativity, and a willingness to learn and adapt as we go. As you’ll explore in the next section, this also requires building a culture of responsibility and ethics within the AI community itself, one that prioritizes the well-being and flourishing of humanity as the ultimate goal of technological progress.

归根结底，为 AI 构建可适应、有效法律框架的关键，是以谦逊、创造与边做边学边调适的态度应对挑战。正如下一节将探讨的，这还要求在 AI 共同体内部建设责任与伦理文化，把人类的福祉与繁荣置于技术进步的终极目标。

Building a Responsible AI Culture 建设负责任的 AI 文化

You’ve seen this throughout the chapter, but allow me to reiterate: the challenges posed by personalized AI are not simply technical or legal in nature, but instead, they are fundamentally shaped by the cultural, social, and ethical contexts in which these systems are developed and deployed. Technological solutionism, often championed as a panacea for societal issues, oversimplifies complex problems by proposing technology as the sole remedy.7 This approach overlooks the intricate web of socio-cultural dynamics that underpin many of these challenges. To truly navigate the complex landscape of AI and ensure that these technologies are used in ways that benefit society as a whole, we need to focus not just on building better algorithms or regulations, but on cultivating a culture of responsibility and ethics within the AI community itself.

本章反复强调一点，请允许我再次重申：个性化 AI 带来的挑战并非单纯技术或法律问题，而是从根本上被这些系统所处的文化、社会与伦理语境所塑造。技术解决主义常被奉为社会问题的万灵药，把技术当作唯一药方，从而过度简化了复杂问题。它忽视了支撑许多挑战的那张错综复杂的社会文化之网。要真正驾驭 AI 的复杂图景、确保这些技术造福全社会，我们不仅要打造更好的算法或法规，更要在 AI 共同体内部培育责任与伦理的文化。

At the heart of this effort is a recognition that the development and deployment of AI is not a neutral or value-free enterprise. The choices we make about what problems to solve, what data to use, and how to design and implement these systems are all deeply shaped by our cultural assumptions, biases, and values. As such, building a responsible AI culture requires a commitment to actively examining and challenging these assumptions and to centering the needs and perspectives of those who are most affected by these technologies.

这一努力的核心，是认识到 AI 的开发与部署绝非中立、无价值的事业。我们选择解决什么问题、使用什么数据、如何设计与实现这些系统，都深受自身文化假设、偏见与价值的塑造。因此，建设负责任的 AI 文化，需要我们主动审视并挑战这些假设，并把受这些技术影响最深者的需求与视角置于中心。

One key aspect of this is promoting greater diversity, equity, and inclusion within the AI field itself. Despite the transformative potential of AI, the community of researchers, developers, and practitioners working on these technologies remains overwhelmingly homogeneous, with women, people of color, and other underrepresented groups often marginalized or excluded from key decision-making roles. This lack of diversity not only limits the range of perspectives and ideas that are brought to bear on the development of AI, but can also perpetuate and amplify existing biases and inequalities.

其中一个关键方面，是在 AI 领域内部推动更大的多元、公平与包容。尽管 AI 具有变革潜力，但从事这些技术的研究者、开发者与从业者群体仍然高度同质化，女性、有色人种及其他代表性不足群体常被边缘化、或被排除在关键决策岗位之外。这种多样性的缺失，不仅限制了投入 AI 开发的视角与思想范围，还可能延续并放大既有的偏见与不平等。

To address this, we need to actively work to create more inclusive and equitable spaces within the AI community and to support and empower underrepresented voices to shape the direction and priorities of the field. This may involve initiatives like mentorship programs, diversity and inclusion training, and targeted efforts to recruit and retain a more diverse workforce. But it also requires a deeper reckoning with the structural and systemic barriers that have long excluded certain groups from full participation in the tech industry, and a willingness to challenge and dismantle these barriers at every level.

为此，我们需要主动在 AI 共同体内创造更包容、更公平的空间，支持并赋能代表性不足的声音去形塑该领域的方向与优先事项。这可能包括导师计划、多元与包容培训，以及更有针对性地招募与留住多元人才。但这还要求我们更深地正视那些长期把某些群体挡在科技业充分参与之外的结构性、系统性壁垒，并愿意在每一个层面挑战、拆除这些壁垒。

Footnote: 7. For interested readers, the book To Save Everything, Click Here: The Folly of Technological Solutionism by Evgeny Morozov (PublicAffairs) is a good reference on this topic.

Another key element of building a responsible AI culture is fostering a greater sense of interdisciplinarity and collaboration across different fields and sectors. The challenges posed by personalized AI are not just technical in nature, but are deeply intertwined with questions of ethics, law, social science, and the humanities. To fully understand these challenges and develop effective solutions, we need to break down the silos that often separate these different domains and create more opportunities for cross-disciplinary dialogue and collaboration.

建设负责任 AI 文化的另一个关键要素，是在不同领域与部门之间培育更强的跨学科与协作意识。个性化 AI 的挑战不仅是技术性的，更与伦理、法律、社会科学及人文学科深度交织。要真正理解这些挑战并拿出有效方案，我们需要打破常把这些领域分隔开来的孤岛，创造更多跨学科对话与协作的机会。

This may involve initiatives like joint research projects, interdisciplinary conferences and workshops, and partnerships among academia, industry, government, and civil society. But it also requires a fundamental shift in the way we think about the role and responsibilities of AI practitioners themselves. Rather than seeing ourselves as narrow technical experts, we need to embrace a more holistic and socially engaged vision of our work, one that recognizes the broader social and ethical implications of the technologies we create and seeks to proactively address them.

这可能包括联合研究项目、跨学科学术会议与工作坊，以及学术界、产业界、政府与公民社会之间的合作。但它也要求我们从根本上转变对 AI 从业者自身角色与责任的认知。我们不应把自己看作狭隘的技术专家，而应拥抱一种更整体、更具社会参与感的工作愿景——认识到所创技术更广泛的社会与伦理意涵，并主动应对它们。

Central to this vision is a commitment to transparency, accountability, and public engagement around the development and deployment of AI systems. Rather than treating AI as an opaque box or a proprietary secret, we need to create more opportunities for public scrutiny, dialogue, and participation in the shaping of these technologies. This may involve initiatives like making key algorithms and datasets open source, creating public forums for feedback and critique, and establishing independent oversight and auditing mechanisms to ensure that AI systems are being developed and used in ways that align with public values and interests.

这一愿景的核心，是围绕 AI 系统的开发与部署坚守透明、问责与公众参与。我们不应把 AI 当作黑箱或专有秘密，而应创造更多让公众监督、对话与参与形塑这些技术的机会。这可能包括将关键算法与数据集开源、设立供反馈与批评的公共论坛，以及建立独立的监督与审计机制，确保 AI 系统的开发与使用契合公共价值与利益。

Building a culture of responsibility in AI is not a one-time effort, but an ongoing process that requires sustained commitment, reflection, and action from all of us who are involved in this field. It means being willing to ask difficult questions, challenge our own assumptions and biases, and prioritize the well-being and flourishing of humanity over narrow technical or commercial interests. And it means recognizing that the true measure of success in AI is not just in the sophistication of our algorithms or the scale of our deployments, but in the positive impact we can have on the lives and societies we serve.

在 AI 中建设责任文化并非一劳永逸，而是一个需要我们所有从业者持续投入、反思与行动的长期过程。它意味着愿意提出尖锐问题、挑战自身的假设与偏见，并把人类的福祉与繁荣置于狭隘技术或商业利益之上。也意味着认识到：AI 成功的真正标尺，不仅在于算法的精巧或部署的规模，更在于我们能对所服务的生活与社会产生的积极影响。

AI Safety Beyond Algorithms: The Human Elements 超越算法的 AI 安全：人的要素

Throughout this chapter, you’ve explored the complex cultural, social, and legal landscapes that shape the development and deployment of personalized AI systems. But as you’ve seen, the challenges and opportunities posed by these technologies are not just a matter of technical design or legal regulation; instead, they are fundamentally intertwined with questions of human values, ethics, and behavior.

本章一路走来，你已探索了形塑个性化 AI 系统发展与部署的复杂文化、社会与法律图景。但正如所见，这些技术带来的挑战与机遇不仅关乎技术设计或法律监管，更从根本上与人类价值、伦理和行为问题交织在一起。

In this final section, I want to focus on the critical importance of centering human factors in our approaches to AI safety and governance. Too often, discussions of AI

在这最后一节，我想强调在 AI 安全与治理路径中“以人为中心”的极端重要性。人们在谈论 AI

— PDF 第 277 页 —

risk and responsibility focus narrowly on the technical aspects of algorithms and systems, as if the challenges posed by these technologies can be solved through better code or more sophisticated machine learning techniques alone. But as you’ve seen throughout this book, the reality is that the risks and benefits of AI are deeply shaped by the social, cultural, and institutional contexts in which these systems are developed and deployed.

风险与责任时，往往狭隘地聚焦于算法与系统的技术层面，仿佛单凭更好的代码或更精巧的机器学习技术就能解决这些技术带来的挑战。但正如全书所见，现实是：AI 的风险与收益，深受这些系统所处的社会、文化与制度语境所塑造。

At the heart of this is a recognition that AI systems are not neutral or objective, but are imbued with the values, assumptions, and biases of their creators and the societies in which they are embedded. From the choice of training data and optimization metrics to the design of user interfaces and deployment contexts, every aspect of an AI system reflects human choices and priorities. As such, ensuring the safety and beneficial impact of these systems requires not just technical solutions, but a deep engagement with the human factors that shape their development and use.

其核心是认识到：AI 系统并非中立、客观，而是浸润着其创造者及其所处社会的价值、假设与偏见。从训练数据与优化指标的选择，到用户界面与部署场景的设计，AI 系统的方方面面都反映着人的选择与优先事项。因此，确保这些系统安全、有益，不仅需要技术方案，更需要深度介入那些塑造其开发与使用的人的要素。

One key aspect of this is recognizing the inherent limitations and uncertainties of AI systems, and the need for ongoing human oversight and judgment in their deployment. No matter how sophisticated our algorithms become, there will always be edge cases, unintended consequences, and value trade-offs that require human discernment and decision making. As such, we need to move beyond the myth of fully autonomous or “superhuman” AI, and instead focus on designing systems that augment and support human intelligence and agency, rather than replacing it entirely.

一个关键方面，是承认 AI 系统固有的局限与不确定性，并在其部署中持续保留人的监督与判断。无论算法多么精巧，总会存在需要人来明辨与决策的边缘情形、意外后果与价值权衡。因此，我们需要超越“完全自主”或“超人” AI 的迷思，转而专注于设计增强、支持人类智能与能动性的系统，而非彻底取代之。

This means creating AI systems that are transparent, interpretable, and accountable to human users and stakeholders. It means building in mechanisms for human oversight and control, such as the ability to override or modify AI outputs, or to provide feedback and guidance to improve system performance over time.8 And it means recognizing that the ultimate responsibility for the impacts of AI systems lies not with the algorithms themselves, but with the human creators, operators, and beneficiaries who shape their development and use.

这意味着打造透明、可解释、对人类用户与利益相关者负责的 AI 系统；意味着内置人的监督与控制机制，例如能够推翻或修改 AI 输出、或随时间提供反馈与指引以改进系统性能；也意味着认识到，对 AI 系统影响负最终责任的不是算法本身，而是塑造其开发与使用的人类创造者、操作者与受益者。

Another key human factor in AI safety is the role of education, training, and public engagement in shaping the responsible development and deployment of these technologies. As AI systems become increasingly ubiquitous and consequential in our lives, it is essential that we foster a greater sense of AI literacy and critical thinking among the general public. This means not just teaching people how to use and interact with AI systems, but empowering them to ask critical questions about the values, assumptions, and potential impacts of these technologies on their lives and communities.

AI 安全中另一个关键的人的要素，是教育、培训与公众参与在形塑这些技术负责任地发展与部署中的作用。随着 AI 系统在生活中愈发普及、影响愈发重大，我们必须在公众中培育更强的 AI 素养与批判性思维。这不仅是教人们如何使用、如何与 AI 系统互动，更是赋能他们去追问这些技术的价值、假设及其对自身生活与社区的潜在影响。

Footnote: 8. As in this Nature paper where the AI learns to defer its decision to doctors when it is not sure: Krishnamurthy Dvijotham et al., “Enhancing the Reliability and Accuracy of AI-Enabled Diagnosis via Complementarity-Driven Deferral to Clinicians,” Nature Medicine 29, no. 7 (2023): 1814–1820, https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-023-02437-x.

— PDF 第 278 页 —

It also means creating more opportunities for public participation and dialogue in the shaping of AI policies and practices. Rather than treating AI development as a matter of narrow technical expertise or corporate strategy, we need to recognize it as a deeply political and social endeavor that affects us all. This means creating forums and mechanisms for public input and deliberation, such as citizen assemblies, stakeholder councils, and participatory design processes, to ensure that the voices and perspectives of diverse communities are heard and taken into account.

这也意味着在形塑 AI 政策与实践中创造更多公众参与与对话的机会。我们不应把 AI 开发当作狭隘的技术专长或企业战略之事，而应认识到它是一项影响我们所有人、深刻政治性与社会性的事业。这意味着创设公民大会、利益相关者委员会、参与式设计等公众输入与审议的论坛与机制，确保多元社区的声音与视角被听到、被纳入考量。

As we continue to navigate the complex and rapidly evolving landscape of personalized AI, let us keep this human-centered perspective at the forefront of our minds and actions. Let us strive to create AI systems that are not just technically sophisticated, but ethically grounded and socially responsible. And let us work together, across boundaries of discipline and sector, to build a future in which the transformative potential of AI is harnessed for the benefit of all humanity, not just a privileged few.

在我们继续穿行于个性化 AI 复杂而快速演进的图景之际，让我们把这种以人为本的视角置于思想与行动的最前沿。让我们努力创造的 AI 系统不仅技术精巧，更有伦理根基、对社会负责。让我们跨越学科与部门的边界携手共建，让 AI 的变革潜力造福全人类，而非少数特权者。

In the end, the true promise of AI lies not in the creation of intelligent machines, but in the cultivation of intelligent, compassionate, and wise human beings. It is only by putting people at the center of our AI efforts, and by working to promote human agency, creativity, and flourishing, that we can hope to create a future in which these powerful technologies are a force for good in the world. So let us take up this challenge with courage, humility, and a deep commitment to the well-being of all. The future of AI, and of humanity itself, depends on it.

归根结底，AI 真正的许诺不在于造出智能机器，而在于培育出智慧、慈悲而明智的人。唯有把人置于 AI 事业的中心、致力于增进人的能动性、创造力与繁荣，我们才有望创造一个让这些强大技术成为世间向善之力的未来。因此，让我们带着勇气、谦逊与对全体福祉的深切担当来迎接这一挑战。AI 的未来，乃至人类自身的未来，都系于此。

Summary 本章小结

In this chapter, you have explored the broader societal context in which privacy-preserving LLMs operate. Key takeaways include:

本章探讨了隐私保护 LLM 所处的更广阔社会语境。要点如下：

  • Generative AI represents a new kind of socio-technical system where technology and society are deeply intertwined.

    生成式 AI 代表一种新型社会技术系统，技术与社会在其中深度交织。

  • AI is mediating cultural evolution through content generation, personalization, and the emergence of algorithmic culture.

    AI 正通过内容生成、个性化与算法文化的兴起，中介着文化演进。

  • Current legal frameworks struggle with AI-specific challenges across copyright, privacy, bias, and liability.

    现行法律框架在版权、隐私、偏见与责任等 AI 特有挑战面前力有不逮。

  • Effective AI governance requires principles-based, adaptive regulatory frameworks that can evolve with technology.

    有效的 AI 治理需要基于原则、可随技术演进的适应性监管框架。

  • Technical solutions must be complemented by cultural change, education, and human oversight.

    技术方案必须辅以文化变革、教育与人的监督。

作为开发隐私保护 LLM 的从业者，我们不仅要应对技术挑战，也要正视这些更广阔的社会意涵。你在落地前几章技术方法时所做的选择，将形塑这些系统对个人与社区的影响。
